name: Jean Grey
bio: Telepath and telekinetic; host of the Phoenix Force. Has died and returned more than any other X-Man, which has made her relationships (especially with Scott and Logan) a recurring site of grief and resurrection.

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: Morrison / Whedon Era
era.description: New X-Men (2001–2004) and Astonishing X-Men (2004–2008). Emma Frost joins, Jean dies, the school becomes a school.

relationships.label: Rivals who respect each other
relationships.summary: A rivalry with uncommon mutual respect. Jean's psychic confrontation with Emma in New X-Men #139 is the high point; by the Krakoan era they are colleagues who occasionally still needle each other about Scott.

events.note: Jean tears through Emma's mind after discovering the affair.

events.issue: Phoenix Resurrection: The Return of Jean Grey #5 (2018)
events.note: Jean's return; Emma among those present.

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: Silver Age (Lee/Kirby/Thomas)
era.description: X-Men #1 (1963) through the original run's cancellation at #66. The first five students and the founding Xavier/Magneto conflict.

relationships.label: First love, marriage, Phoenix, death
relationships.summary: The franchise's central romance. A shy mutual crush in 1963 became the marriage in X-Men #30 (1994), was broken by Jean's death as Dark Phoenix, by her resurrection, by Scott's psychic affair with Emma Frost, and by Jean's second death. Her Krakoan return left them cordial co-workers rather than a couple.

events.note: Scott's unspoken feelings for Jean are established in the first issue.
Dark Phoenix Saga ends with Jean's suicide on the Moon to stop herself.
Jean discovers Scott's psychic affair with Emma.
Jean is killed by Xorn/Magneto; she tells Scott to live.

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: Claremont Era
era.description: Giant-Size X-Men #1 (1975) through Chris Claremont's departure after X-Men #3 (1991). The all-new team, Phoenix, Days of Future Past, the Brood, Inferno.

relationships.label: Unrequited, mostly
relationships.summary: Logan's attraction to Jean is written as intense and almost never acted on; Jean's response varies by writer from fond refusal to genuine temptation. The relationship is largely about restraint, and it is consummated only in alternate futures.

events.note: Logan's interest in Jean is first made explicit.
Stranded on Asteroid M, Jean and Logan kiss; Logan kills her so the Phoenix will take over and save them.
Phoenix-Jean seeks out Logan; he refuses her repeatedly.

continuity.name: Earth-616

era.name: Silver Age (Lee/Kirby/Thomas)
era.description: X-Men #1 (1963) through the original run's cancellation at #66. The first five students and the founding Xavier/Magneto conflict.

relationships.label: Mentor, with a buried complication
relationships.summary: Xavier trained Jean's telepathy from childhood. X-Men #3 (1964) briefly gave him secret romantic feelings for her, a thread later writers abandoned and then treated as evidence of his ethical blind spots.

events.note: A thought balloon reveals Xavier's attraction to Jean; it is never pursued.
Jean's Phoenix return; Xavier's role in suppressing her power earlier is part of the backstory.

era.name: Claremont Era
era.description: Giant-Size X-Men #1 (1975) through Chris Claremont's departure after X-Men #3 (1991). The all-new team, Phoenix, Days of Future Past, the Brood, Inferno.

relationships.label: The team's two matriarchs
relationships.summary: Close from the start of the new team; Storm was Jean's closest female friend through the Phoenix years and held the team together in her absences.

events.note: Jean becomes Phoenix; Storm is at her side.
Returned Jean recruits Storm first for her new team.

continuity.name: Earth-1610 (Ultimate)
continuity.description: The original Ultimate Marvel universe (2000–2015), a modern-day reboot with younger characters.

era.name: Morrison / Whedon Era
era.description: New X-Men (2001–2004) and Astonishing X-Men (2004–2008). Emma Frost joins, Jean dies, the school becomes a school.

relationships.label: Teenage version
relationships.summary: In the Ultimate universe they are teenagers, the romance is more volatile, and Jean briefly chooses Wolverine. Included as a continuity contrast to the 616 marriage.

events.note: Scott and Jean established as a couple at Xavier's.
Jean leaves Scott for Logan, briefly.
